title.narrative: Advocacy plan developed

description.narrative: An advocacy document has been drafted for members of the working group, network and individuals presentinga guide for advocacy for the work on the project. Advocacy plan is written on 50 pages format A4 and consists of the following:Advocacy plan priorities;Advocacy plan objectives;The list of mapped actors of the advocacy process with their contact information.The advocacy plan has one general objective and 6 specific objectives. General objective of the advocacy plan is to increase the level of protection of the rights of citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina to freedom of opinion and expression, the right to freedom of peaceful assembly and the right to freedom of movement in relation to security institutions and the level of legal security of the defendant.Specific objectives of the advocacy plan are:Specific objective 1: To amend the cantonal Laws on Public Order and Peace in the Federation of BiH, the Law on Public Order and Peace of the Brko District of BiH and the Law on Public Order and Peace of the Republic of Srpska.Specific objective 2: To amend the laws on public gatherings in Bosnia and Herzegovina at all levels.Specific objective 3: To amend the decisions on determining the space for holding public gatherings of the Assembly of the City of Banja Luka from December 2011 (Official Gazette 31/11).Specific objective 4: To amend the provisions concerning emergency measures for the prevention and control of communicable diseases of the Law on Protection of the Population from Infectious Diseases and the Law on Protection and Rescue of People and Material Goods in Emergencies at all levels in BiH.Specific objective 5: To amend the provisions of the misdemeanour legislation in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Brko District of Bosnia and Herzegovina, concerning the review of the factual description of the request to initiate misdemeanour proceedings / misdemeanour order requesting a court decision.Specific objective 6: To contribute to the adoption of guidelines by the courts and the police to improve the practices of security institutions in the following areas:Application of police powers in cases of peaceful assembly;Application of means of coercion against perpetrators of offenses in the field of public order and peace;Practicing the skills of legal reasoning and argumentation;Methodology of discovering and proving the socalled fake news.Beside detail specific objectives of the advocacy process,the plan contains description of activities, success indicator, responsible persons/organizations, advocacy targets, deadlines and remarks (if needed) for each specific advocacy objective.

title.narrative: Implemented five training sessions

description.narrative: In order to adequately conduct the future advocacy campaign, taking into account that networked academic institutions do not have experience in these processes, five trainings will be conducted on the advocacy unitsthematic. The aim of this activity is to strengthen the capacities of academic institutions to be more proactive in expressing their views on events in everyday life in the community regarding human rights violations. Also, these trainings will further strengthen the connection between the members of the network and especially the CSOs and the academic community. This is especially important if we take into account that the addressed improvements refer to security institutions that are not sensitive to civil crime and actions of this type. This is supported by the fact that the people behind the academic community, CSOs and human rights defenders will be a kind of spokespersons for both institutions and the public, who will represent and express the views of the network. Training topics will be: advocacy process, negotiation process, public speaking, policy dialogue and public consultations, use of research as an advocacy tool, networking and work within network, and others that are needed due to the composition of the network. These trainings will be implemented by a Co Applicant and a human rights expert who will be hired by Co Applicant. The trainings will be realized in 5 different locations with about 20 people each. The methodological approach used during the trainings will be adapted to adult education, with adequate andragogical and lifelong learning methods. The Outputs of this project activity will be prepared and developed adequate training material and implemented five training session.The realization of this output is predicted for the next period. However, in order to provide favourable conditions for achieving this outcome in the second year of project implementation during December 2021, an invitation letter was prepared for participation in the first training to be held on February 4th, 2022 in East Sarajevo. Also, a training agenda was developed with the aim of strengthening the capacities of representatives of the academic community and civil society organizations in the implementation of public advocacy actions within the CAHR project. An invitation letter for the first training, as well as the training program, was sent to interested civil society organizations and academic institutions, in order to provide an adequate number of participants in this training in a timely manner.

title.narrative: Five public consultation sessions related to violations of freedom of movement implemented

description.narrative: Like the previous two activities, this activity addresses the dialogue of relevant actors in local community units where the ban on movement and the violation of human rights to freedom of movement have been noted.
